trigger: Observed tail decline in 2018-10 versus 2018-07; only 4 orders in the final observed month.
hypothesis: H1 seller count collapse
evidence_for: Final tail reports nan active sellers versus 1278 in 2018-08.
evidence_against: The tail is a partial observation and is excluded by the complete-period rule.
business_magnitude: edge-month GMV is 0.00 versus 854686.33 in the prior complete month
decision: gate executive reporting on completeness

trigger: Observed tail decline in 2018-10 versus 2018-07; only 4 orders in the final observed month.
hypothesis: H2 seller productivity collapse
evidence_for: Observed GMV per seller is not interpretable in the four-order tail.
evidence_against: Complete months retain normal seller productivity; the denominator itself is incomplete.
decision: do not escalate commercial action from the tail

trigger: Observed tail decline in 2018-10 versus 2018-07; only 4 orders in the final observed month.
hypothesis: H3 AOV collapse
evidence_for: Tail AOV is 0.00, driven by four orders.
evidence_against: AOV is computed on an ineligible partial period.
decision: flag partial periods

trigger: Observed tail decline in 2018-10 versus 2018-07; only 4 orders in the final observed month.
hypothesis: H4 data incompleteness
evidence_for: The last observed months fail the documented complete-month rule.
evidence_against: No raw row-level check can prove the upstream extract's intended end date.
alternative_explanation: legitimate seasonality cannot be ruled out without current data
decision: enforce a period-completeness gate

trigger: Actionable origins show different conversion rates and sparse groups have wide uncertainty.
hypothesis: H1 optimize raw MQL volume alone
evidence_for: MQL volume and conversion rank different origins; social contributes 1,350 MQLs but converts at 5.6%.
evidence_against: Volume is not downstream value and unknown is not actionable.
business_magnitude: paid vs social gap is 6.7 percentage points
decision: use a multidimensional channel scorecard

trigger: Actionable origins show different conversion rates and sparse groups have wide uncertainty.
hypothesis: H2 origin is associated with conversion
evidence_for: Global origin test and FDR-adjusted pairwise tests provide evidence of conversion differences.
evidence_against: Effect size is modest and does not establish causal channel quality.
alternative_explanation: selection bias, linkage and unmeasured seller mix
decision: separate acquisition efficiency from retention claims

trigger: Actionable origins show different conversion rates and sparse groups have wide uncertainty.
hypothesis: H3 origin-specific retention advantage is established
evidence_for: M3 retention CI table is eligibility-aware.
evidence_against: The adjusted retention model and global M3 test do not provide strong evidence of origin-specific retention intervention.
decision: do not optimize channels on M3 retention alone

trigger: Median first-sale time is 44 days and activation by 30 days is 34.2% among valid links.
hypothesis: H1 seller onboarding has a long time-to-value
evidence_for: Activation timing distribution and cumulative curve show a delayed first sale.
evidence_against: Historical data does not identify which onboarding step caused delay.
alternative_explanation: seller readiness, category and demand differences
decision: instrument 7/30/60-day onboarding checkpoints

trigger: Median first-sale time is 44 days and activation by 30 days is 34.2% among valid links.
hypothesis: H2 faster activation is associated with stronger M3 retention
evidence_for: M3 retention rates decline across activation-speed buckets after the small ≤7d bucket.
evidence_against: The comparison is observational and extreme buckets are small.
decision: test onboarding interventions with retention as guardrail

trigger: Median first-sale time is 44 days and activation by 30 days is 34.2% among valid links.
hypothesis: H3 origin alone explains activation speed
evidence_for: Activation speed varies by origin in the CI table.
evidence_against: Origin is not the same as seller readiness or onboarding experience.
decision: target the onboarding journey rather than a channel proxy

trigger: Top 20% of sellers account for 82.7% of seller GMV proxy.
hypothesis: H1 marketplace value is concentrated
evidence_for: Lorenz/Gini and top-share statistics show a long-tailed seller distribution.
evidence_against: Concentration is measured on historical positive-GMV sellers, not current supply health.
decision: monitor top 1/5/10/20% shares

trigger: Top 20% of sellers account for 82.7% of seller GMV proxy.
hypothesis: H2 generic seller diversification is the right immediate action
evidence_for: High concentration creates dependency risk.
evidence_against: The evidence does not identify which categories or states are fragile.
alternative_explanation: some concentration may reflect healthy specialization
decision: target categories with high GMV and weak seller breadth

trigger: Top 20% of sellers account for 82.7% of seller GMV proxy.
hypothesis: H3 concentration is stable across time and segments
evidence_for: Monthly and category concentration tables permit the check.
evidence_against: Historical scope does not establish a universal threshold or causal driver.
decision: use a monitoring trigger, not an arbitrary threshold

trigger: Late orders have lower reviews and a higher low-review rate than on-time orders.
hypothesis: H1 delivery lateness is associated with customer-experience deterioration
evidence_for: Mean review penalty is -1.73 points and low-review risk ratio is 5.87x.
evidence_against: Association is not causal proof.
alternative_explanation: category, state, freight and review selection
decision: prioritize operational investigation by volume × severity × penalty

trigger: Late orders have lower reviews and a higher low-review rate than on-time orders.
hypothesis: H2 delay severity has a dose-response pattern
evidence_for: Severity buckets retain monotonic operational detail and show the late tail's weaker review outcomes.
evidence_against: Early/late buckets are observational and some extremes are smaller.
business_magnitude: late >14d is the most severe diagnostic segment
decision: investigate severity bands before a broad rollout

trigger: Late orders have lower reviews and a higher low-review rate than on-time orders.
hypothesis: H3 one seller is the root cause
evidence_for: Seller-level responsibility is not available for multi-seller orders without attribution assumptions.
evidence_against: Order-level evidence should not assign blame to a single seller.
business_magnitude: seller attribution is a measurement limitation
alternative_explanation: carrier, route, category and customer geography
decision: do not assign seller blame from this dataset

trigger: Selected high-value category cool_stuff falls 46.5% from 2018-07 to 2018-08 while retaining sufficient historical volume.
hypothesis: H1 category demand/GMV deterioration
evidence_for: The category is selected using material GMV, sufficient orders and complete-month decline.
evidence_against: Historical category trend is not a current commercial forecast.
decision: build a category-specific diagnostic plan

trigger: Selected high-value category cool_stuff falls 46.5% from 2018-07 to 2018-08 while retaining sufficient historical volume.
hypothesis: H2 orders versus AOV explains the category movement
evidence_for: Category tables separate GMV, orders and AOV/productivity proxies.
evidence_against: Decomposition is descriptive and may not capture assortment changes.
alternative_explanation: price, assortment and promotion data are unavailable
decision: choose an intervention only after driver split

trigger: Selected high-value category cool_stuff falls 46.5% from 2018-07 to 2018-08 while retaining sufficient historical volume.
hypothesis: H3 seller breadth/productivity explains the decline
evidence_for: Active sellers and GMV per seller are tracked by category.
evidence_against: Seller attribution is item-based and multi-seller order context remains limited.
business_magnitude: seller breadth and productivity must be compared
decision: monitor category seller breadth and productivity

trigger: Selected high-value category cool_stuff falls 46.5% from 2018-07 to 2018-08 while retaining sufficient historical volume.
hypothesis: H4 category experience explains the decline
evidence_for: Category late rate and review metrics are available for further investigation.
evidence_against: No causal demand model is available.
business_magnitude: customer-experience gap is a guardrail, not invented lost GMV
decision: keep CX in the category decision card as a guardrail
